catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 requires the output fields reached and joint_positions and allows block/duration_s. The pinned MovJ service is a queued command whose response is only int32 res and the controller queue id in robot_return; it reports neither arrival nor measured joint positions and has no block or duration field. Binding the class would invent a completion claim and unmapped inputs.

cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 requires reached and a frame and allows duration_s. The pinned MovL service is a queued command returning only int32 res and a queue id; it has no frame field, no completion signal and no measured position. The class would require inventing an arrival claim and a frame the service does not accept.

cap.motion.stop.v1 takes a deceleration and requires a stopped/stopped-position output. The pinned Stop.srv has an empty request and returns only int32 res; the callback sends Stop() and does not report a stopping position or zero velocity. Using the class would invent a deceleration input and a stopped-state measurement.

No catalogue class expresses enabling or re-arming a robot arm from an input-free service. cap.device.configure.v1 is a resource-state write, while the pinned EnableRobot service performs the native re-arm and is the one action declared reenable=True (CORE-086).

notes:
PASSED the fake gate with no findings or warnings (G1-G9). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's family is python-object with PythonObjectDriver and entry symbol dobot_demo.demo:adderClient (confirmed at dobot_demo/dobot_demo/demo.py:10). That Python class exposes only initialization, point and set_do and has no stop, fault, state or connection method, so it cannot express the device's safe stop; the device interface is a ROS 2 graph of services and feedback topics on the pinned C++ node. This package is a configuration-only RosDriver over that graph (no invented Python native), with every binding cited to the pinned clone. The demo remains the card's entry symbol, but it is not the hardware transport. SCOPE: reads of /joint_states, dobot_msgs_v4/msg/ToolVectorActual and dobot_msgs_v4/msg/RobotStatus; MovJ joint mode (mode=true, rad converted to deg), MovL Cartesian mode (mode=false, mm unchanged and orientation rad converted to deg), Stop and EnableRobot. The stop and safe-state bindings are the same fixed Stop() request (CORE-074); the e-stop therefore sends it once. NOT COVERED: SpeedFactor, DO/Digital IO, ServoJ/ServoP, MoveJog, Pause/Continue, EmergencyStop service, ClearError, DisableRobot, PowerOn, Modbus, tool/user frame commands, MoveIt action clients, Gazebo/MoveIt simulation, kinematics, safety-skin and collision configuration, and GetPose/GetAngle (the feedback topics are used instead). The service prefix is the default single-robot one; robot_number > 1 prefixes every service name with robot_node_name + '/' and is not bound. Rosbridge is an operator deployment assumption: the upstream node is native ROS 2, and the operator must run rosbridge and the node; the endpoint is not in the clone. Nothing here ran on a live ROS graph or an arm. QUEUE SEMANTICS: MovJ and MovL are queue commands; the receipt reports accepted=true and the controller queue id from robot_return, never reached or arrival. A move's effect on the real device appears later in the feedback topics. The fake updates its published joint positions or tool pose as soon as the service is accepted, so its TCAP-003 effect is a fake property, not a completion claim. LIMITS: the clone serves CR3/CR5/CR7/CR10/CR12/CR16/CR20/CR30H, CR10AF, E6/ME6, Nova2 and Nova5 and states no joint travel, Cartesian workspace or orientation range. Every move input is Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay only, and until the operator supplies site-limits.json every move is refused with MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. SAFETY: risk is R2 (six-axis arm), above the card floor R0. The safe state is the controller's acknowledged Stop() dashboard command, reached through the fixed /dobot_bringup_ros2/srv/Stop service; it is both safety_bindings.estop and the input-free safe_state=True action, and the strict resolve accepts the achieved_by route for SAFE-045. No estop_physical_ref is claimed: the clone contains no independent physical emergency-stop text. The acknowledgement is not a measured stopped position or zero velocity, and the clone does not show that Stop() clears every queued command or another client's motion. There is no reset hook: a reset only releases the MHS latch (SAFE-042), and EnableRobot is the one input-free reenable=True action (CORE-086); EnableRobot() is documented to enable the robot, but the clone does not state that it clears faults or releases an EmergencyStop. RESIDUAL UPSTREAM RISK: the dashboard command loop polls a zero-timeout read until it sees ';' with no overall deadline (dobot_bringup_v4/src/command.cpp:128-140), and main.cpp runs a single-threaded spin_some, so a lost dashboard reply can block the node's callbacks and delay or prevent a later Stop service; the bridge then reports an unknown/unreached safe state and keeps the latch, so no false safe state is committed in that case. The reply parser sets res only when a '{' is found (dobot_bringup_v4/src/command.cpp:142-152); a malformed brace-less reply leaves the ROS int32 res at 0 and can satisfy the res==0 predicate, which the clone does not distinguish. A well-formed controller reply that carries an error id is refused. The fake exercises the declared service failure and a missing-res reply through the actual native estop path; the native bridge cannot see the text parser's brace-less case. READS: when the feedback connection is down the node republishes the last valid joint positions or zeros and publishes no stopped flag (dobot_bringup_v4/src/main.cpp:50-59); ToolVectorActual is published only while connected. These are observations, not stopped-state evidence. FAKE: fake.py is an ROS-free analytic stand-in, not a recording and not the upstream node or simulator; it runs no TCP, ROS graph, kinematics or queue, moves instantly, and every number and failure switch is marked placeholder. It is F0 contract evidence only, never an MHS-Device level. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. The clone was left unmodified; no network, pip install, upstream import or hardware run was used. This package is model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model identity and reviewed_by stays null. The loader refuses the hardware backend at R2 until a human signs it, and RosDriver refuses every hardware backend without a human hardware review; fake evidence establishes neither a real ROS run nor a hardware run. The final gate run after the last driver, fake and facts edits again exited 0 and printed the same digest.

MODEL REVIEW (gpt-6.1-sol, a model and not a human, 2026-11-17; reviewed_by stays null): Model review traced Stop through the formatter, callback, callRosService and doTcpCmd: a swallowed TCP exception or brace-less reply can leave res=0, so the same ROS response cannot establish controller acknowledgement; the original false success was reproduced with a package fake. Updated driver.py, fake.py, facts.md and test_driver.py to remove the unproven safety binding/flag, report only service_returned, model the indistinguishable failure and nonzero-code refusal, correct ROS message/response shapes and narrow or repair citations; regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. All 11 package-specific cases pass, including failed e-stop with latch refusal and nonzero native return codes without effects; the stock gate correctly refuses the hardware view at G3 STRICT SAFE-045 and NO_ESTOP. Strict collection reports RESULT_UNTRUSTED until the orchestrator records the block; the RosDriver route also requires the proposed registry correction. For the human reviewer: Unblocking needs a native stop/confirmation path that distinguishes transport/parser failure, plus the required physical-stop/deployment review. Stop.srv exposes only res, while command.cpp:157-160 suppresses errors and :221-228 returns true; a binding-only predicate cannot repair it. The dashboard receive loop has no overall deadline and can block spin_some, delaying later Stop calls. Removing the safety binding means e-stop latches but sends no dashboard Stop; existing arm motion can continue. An explicit reset only releases the latch. Joint feedback can be stale/zero and ToolVectorActual silent while disconnected. Default single-robot/root namespace only; the Python demo, MoveIt and multi-robot launch paths are not served. No live ROS graph or hardware was run.
